explanation: Compared against WOWII 327 (Wayback all.html; defs 49, 7, 94, 99): for simple connected G with n > 1, if 3γ(G) = γ_i(G) (the independent domination number) then G is well totally dominated. The statement negates the universal claim over finite connected graphs, using dominationNumber, indepDominationNumber and IsWellTotallyDominated (all minimal total dominating sets have equal size). The documented 12-vertex counterexample checks out by hand: γ = 2 via {u,v}; every independent dominating set has 6 vertices (e.g. {u, b₀,…,b₄}); and {u,v} and {v,b₀,b₃} are minimal total dominating sets of different sizes. A formal proof is linked. Dropping n > 1 is irrelevant for a negation. Faithful.
